special_formulas.description: Limit on financial costs for companies other than financial institutions
special_formulas.act_name: Inland Revenue Amendment Act No. 10 of 2021
special_formulas.quote: The limit shall be computed according to the following formula: - A -- X C B Where: ‘A’ = financial cost of the year; ‘B’ = value of financial instruments on which the financial cost incurred during the year; and ‘C’= 4 x total of the issued share capital and reserves of the company as at the end of the year.

special_formulas.description: Limit on financial costs deduction for companies (other than financial institutions) calculated using formula A/B x C.
special_formulas.act_name: Inland Revenue Amendment Act No. 10 of 2021
special_formulas.quote: “(1) The amount of financial costs deducted in calculating the income of a company (other than a financial institution) which is incorporated in or outside Sri Lanka and having an issued share capital as at the date on which the year of assessment ends, from conducting a business or investment for a year of assessment commencing from April l, 2021, shall not exceed the limit referred to in subsection (2). (2) The limit shall be computed according to the following formula: - A -- X C B Where: ‘A’ = financial cost of the year; ‘B’ = value of financial instruments on which the financial cost incurred during the year; and ‘C’= 4 x total of the issued share capital and reserves of the company as at the end of the year.”.

special_formulas.description: Unrelieved loss from business taxed at same rate as current year if it would have been a taxable profit.
special_formulas.act_name: Inland Revenue Amendment Act No. 10 of 2021
special_formulas.quote: “in calculating exempt amounts. For the purpose of this subsection, where any company has an unrelieved loss from business to deduct in the current year of assessment from a period during which that company had operated as a small and medium enterprise and, if- (a) the unrelieved loss was a profit in the year of assessment in which that unrelieved loss was incurred and which would have been taxed at a reduced rate; and (b) the current year business income is not taxable at the same reduced rate as in the year referred to in the paragraph (a), that unrelieved loss shall, (subject to paragraph (b) of subsection (1)), be deemed to be a loss (if it would have been a taxable profit) taxed at the same rate of the current year.”.

special_formulas.description: Gains and profits from specific activities taxed at 14%
special_formulas.act_name: Inland Revenue Amendment Act No. 10 of 2021
special_formulas.quote:
“(5) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary
in the provisions of subparagraph (1A), an
individual’s following gains and profits shall be

(a)
consideration received in respect of

(b)

special_formulas.description: The total of the Capital allowances granted and calculated under the Fourth Schedule to this Act in respect of a depreciable asset shall not exceed the cost of such depreciable asset in any circumstances.
special_formulas.act_name: Inland Revenue Amendment Act No. 45 of 2022
special_formulas.quote:
“(3A) The total of the Capital allowances granted
and calculated under the Fourth Schedule to this
Act in respect of a depreciable asset shall not exceed
the cost of such depreciable asset in any
circumstances.”.

special_formulas.description: Retirement payments received at the time of retirement from employment are exempt if contributions were taxed in a previous year.
special_formulas.act_name: Inland Revenue Amendment Act No. 45 of 2022
special_formulas.quote: “(g) any retirement payments received at the time of the retirement from employment, subject to the condition that the respective retirement contributions have already been considered for income tax purposes and the employee has paid tax on such contributions in a previous year of assessment.”.

special_formulas.description: Rate change for item (a) of sub-paragraph (2) of paragraph 1 of the First Schedule
special_formulas.value: 10% prior to the date on which the provisions referred to in subsection (2) of section 1 come into operation; and 15% with effect from the date on which the provisions referred to in subsection (2) of section 1 come into operation
special_formulas.act_name: Inland Revenue Amendment Act No. 11 of 2026
special_formulas.quote: “at the rate of – (i) 10%, prior to the date on which the provisions referred to in subsection (2) of section 1 come into operation; and (ii) 15%, with effect from the date on which the provisions referred to in subsection (2) of section 1 come into operation;”

special_formulas.description: Deduction of expenses incurred during the year in the production of income from business or investment.
special_formulas.quote: In calculating a person’s income from a business or investment for a year of assessment, expenses to the extent they are incurred during the year by the person and in the production of income from the business or investment, shall be deducted.

special_formulas.description: No deduction for expenses of a capital nature.
special_formulas.quote: No deduction shall be allowed under subsection (1) for an expense of a capital nature.

special_formulas.description: Definition of 'expense of a capital nature'.
special_formulas.quote: In this section, “expense of a capital nature” includes an expense that secures a benefit capable of lasting longer than twelve months.

special_formulas.description: Capital allowances and balancing allowances are deducted in calculating a person's income from a business for a year of assessment.
special_formulas.quote: (1) For the purposes of calculating a person’s income from a business for a year of assessment – (a) the Capital allowances referred to in subsection (2) shall be deducted; and (b) the balancing allowances referred to in subsection (4) shall be deducted;

special_formulas.description: The withholdee of a payment that is not a final withholding payment shall be treated as having paid any tax withheld from the payment or paid with respect to the payment in accordance with subsection (3) or (4) of section 86.
special_formulas.quote: The withholdee of a payment that is not a final withholding payment shall be treated as having paid any tax – (a) withheld from the payment under this Division; or (b) paid with respect to the payment in accordance with subsection (3) or (4) of section 86.

special_formulas.description: A withholdee shall be entitled to a tax credit in an amount equal to the tax treated as paid under subsection (1) for the year of assessment in which the payment is derived.
special_formulas.quote: A withholdee shall be entitled to a tax credit in an amount equal to the tax treated as paid under subsection (1) for the year of assessment in which the payment is derived.

special_formulas.description: Instalment payer may assume current estimated tax payable is equal to previous year increased by 5% uplift.
special_formulas.quote: the instalment payer may assume that its current estimated tax payable for that year of assessment is equal to the amount of tax that was payable by the instalment payer in the previous year of assessment, increased by an uplift of five percent.

special_formulas.description: No tax by quarterly instalments if no tax payable in previous year.
special_formulas.quote: A person shall not be required to pay tax by quarterly instalments under section 90 where that person had no tax payable in the previous year of assessment.

special_formulas.description: Gains from realisation of investment assets taxed at 10%.
special_formulas.quote: those gains from the realisation of investment assets shall be taxed at the rate of 10%

special_formulas.description: Business income from betting, gaming, liquor, or tobacco taxed at 40%.
special_formulas.quote: the type of business income referred to in subparagraph (4) shall be taxed at 40%

special_formulas.description: Remainder of individual's taxable income taxed at rates in subparagraph (1).
special_formulas.quote: only the remainder of the individual’s taxable income shall be taxed at the rates referred to in subparagraph (1)

special_formulas.description: Tax rate for dividends where a person's taxable income includes gains and profits from dividends for the second six months of the year of assessment commencing on April 1, 2022.
special_formulas.quote: “13. Tax rate for dividends Notwithstanding the provisions in other paragraphs of this Schedule, where a person’s taxable income includes gains and profits from dividends for the second six months of the year of assessment commencing on April 1, 2022, such gains and profits shall be taxed at the rate of 15%.”.
